\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Borell --- Definitions: Results}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian halfspace stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p015-b001}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b003,
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b004
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
For real parameters $\rho$ and $\alpha$, define the Gaussian halfspace stability to be
$0$ when $\alpha\leq 0$, to be $1$ when $1\leq\alpha$, and otherwise to be the standard
bivariate Gaussian probability that both coordinates $X$ and $\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y$
are at most the standard Gaussian quantile at $\alpha$, where $X$ and $Y$ are
independent standard Gaussian random variables.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian bivariate stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateStability}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{
  pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p004-b001,
  pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p015-b001
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002,
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b004
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateStability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
For real parameters $\rho,\alpha,\beta$, define the Gaussian bivariate stability as the
probability that independent standard Gaussian random variables $X,Y$ satisfy
$\Phi(X)\leq\alpha$ and $\Phi(\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)\leq\beta$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard Gaussian cumulative distribution function.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian bivariate slope]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateSlope}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateSlope}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
For real numbers $\rho,a,b$, define the Gaussian bivariate slope to be the standard
Gaussian cumulative distribution function evaluated at
\[
\frac{\Phi^{-1}(b)-\rho\,\Phi^{-1}(a)}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}},
\]
where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian cumulative distribution function and $\Phi^{-1}$
is its quantile function.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian bivariate density]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateDensity}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p013-b001}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateDensity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
For real parameters $\rho,a,b$, define the Gaussian bivariate density by
$I(a)\,\phi\!\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(b)-\rho\Phi^{-1}(a)}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}\right)/\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$,
where $I$ is the Gaussian isoperimetric function, $\phi$ is the standard Gaussian
density, and $\Phi^{-1}$ is the standard Gaussian quantile function.
\end{definition}
